ladder.d: People write code and docs on laptops, like any tech company.
People paste short code snippets from early chatbots into their editors.
Agents write and edit code on their own, sometimes whole files.
Agents run code themselves and hand hours of work to other agents.
Agents might build and train models themselves. Then Claude could be improved by Claude.

futures.d: The curves turn out to be S curves, or compute, chips and power become the limit. Today's AI still spreads through the economy. Anthropic thinks this is unlikely, and it gives the most time to adapt.
AI development becomes mostly automated, but humans still set directions and judge results. Anthropic says the evidence points here, with new bottlenecks such as human code review.
AI designs and refines its successors. Progress is set by compute. Small misalignments could compound as models build models, and this is the future Anthropic is least certain about.

caveats.d: Many of the lab figures come from Anthropic about itself. They are useful because nobody else can see inside, but no outside group has checked them yet. Anthropic says it plans to bring in independent evaluators.

caveats.t: Lines of code are not progress
caveats.d: Anthropic says the 8x code per engineer figure is almost certainly an overstatement of the real productivity gain, because it counts quantity, not quality.
Some ratings were made by Claude judging Claude's work. Anthropic checked a sample against staff ratings: within one level 97% of the time.
A straight line on a log chart can turn into an S curve. Chips, power or a missing idea could slow things down. A trend is a guide, not a promise.
The expert survey asks people to guess. Guesses moved 13 years in one year, which tells you how uncertain everyone is.
